extracted.intended_audience: press photographers, photojournalists, photo editors, editors and publishers (news media)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for ethical image editing, use of AI, and editorial oversight in press photography to ensure images remain honest, accurate, and not misleading. Covers acceptable technical corrections, explicit prohibitions on manipulative practices, AI-specific rules, and publisher responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and accuracy of the photograph
rubrics_metrics.description: The photo must remain an honest and accurate visual testimony to reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The integrity of press photography is based on the audience’s confidence that the image represents reality as it took place. Any manipulation that alters this reality can mislead viewers, distort narratives, and damage credibility. Always ensure edits do not change factual content or meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Exposure Compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjusting brightness, contrast, highlights, and shadows to replicate what the human eye perceived at the time of shooting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These corrections ensure viewers can see details lost to under- or overexposure. Adjustments must be made moderately, without exaggerating or obscuring elements of the photo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to color balance and white balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Correcting color temperature and white balance so skin tones, environmental influences, and important details appear natural and true-to-life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to remove ambient lighting color casts that would distort true colors; intended to maintain an accurate representation of the original scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cropping for composition (ethical cropping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cropping to enhance composition and focus on the main subject while removing distracting peripheral elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical cropping must not remove context that changes the meaning of the image. The crop should never hide or omit important information that could mislead the viewer about the nature or extent of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharpness and clarity adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancements to make an image appear crisp and focused, especially for print or digital display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharpening should preserve the natural appearance of the image and avoid introducing artificial edges or textures that were not present in the original shot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noise reduction and lens correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Gentle noise reduction for low-light/high-ISO images and correction of lens defects such as distortion or vignetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noise reduction should improve quality without compromising details. Lens correction should ensure the image remains true to what was seen while correcting known equipment limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of dust stains and sensor artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing minor technical defects (e.g., dust on the sensor) that are not part of the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing these technical flaws is acceptable as long as the editing does not remove actual visual content that was part of the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation of edits (avoid exaggeration or obscuring)
rubrics_metrics.description: All technical adjustments must be made moderately and must not exaggerate, obscure, or otherwise alter elements of the original scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive adjustments that change mood, apparent reality, or salient details cross the line from technical correction to manipulation. Moderate changes replicate what the photographer saw rather than inventing new content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on adding or removing elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserting, deleting, or cloning parts of the image to change what was captured is unethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insert or remove subjects, objects, or details. Such changes change the factual content and mislead viewers; they betray audience trust and can have serious consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on staging of scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructing subjects to behave unnaturally so that the camera creates a certain narrative is unethical for press photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid directing or staging events to manufacture a story. Staging converts documentary photography into constructed imagery and undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on overprocessing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying extreme filters or edits that dramatically change the mood, tone, or apparent reality of the scene is unethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overprocessing (e.g., heavy artistic filters, dramatic tonal changes) can misrepresent events and should be avoided in news/documentary contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misleading captions or cropping
rubrics_metrics.description: Cropping images or writing captions that misrepresent the image or remove essential context is unethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions must accurately describe what is shown and cropping must not alter the viewer’s understanding of the scene. Misleading context damages trust and may have legal or reputational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between AI-powered/illustrative images and authentic press photography
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-powered images used for illustration or design must be clearly distinguished from authentic press photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an important distinction between AI-generated/AI-manipulated imagery and documentary photography. AI can be acceptable for non-news features, design elements, or simulations, but must never be passed off as an authentic photographic record of real events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable applications of AI in journalistic work
rubrics_metrics.description: Using AI for illustrative purposes in non-news features, visual design elements (backgrounds, cover photos), or training/simulation/education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated images may be used for opinion pieces, thematic articles, decorative graphics, or workshops provided they are clearly labeled as such and do not mislead readers about real-world events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable applications of AI in press photography
rubrics_metrics.description: Using AI to create or present images as authentic news photography, to create fictional images representing real events, or to alter historical/factual reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share AI-generated content as authentic news photography. Do not generate or alter images to represent events that never happened or to change the factual record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory disclosure when AI is used
rubrics_metrics.description: Any use of AI-generated images must always include clear disclosure to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency ensures readers can distinguish documentary evidence from illustrative or artistic content. Disclosures should accompany images and explain the nature/origin of the image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and publisher responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and publishers must ensure all images meet ethical standards through policies and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should request full disclosure of all edits applied to images, conduct regular audits of submitted photos, provide ongoing ethics training for employees and freelancers, and maintain strong editorial oversight to protect integrity and audience trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and integrity to maintain audience trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency about edits, provenance, and use of AI is essential to preserve audience confidence in press images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Betraying audience expectations that images represent reality erodes trust and can damage reputations or have legal consequences; rebuilding trust is difficult, so transparency and integrity must be central to practice.
